title: Class Sheet — Fractions
intro: The questions from this week's sheet, one step at a time. Remember: **“of” means ×**, and always ask **“a fraction of WHAT?”**

questions.text:
Un berger a perdu le [[1/7]] de ses 56 chèvres l'an dernier et le [[1/6]] du reste cette année.
a) Quelle fraction de ses chèvres lui reste-t-il ?
hints: How much of the flock is left after the FIRST loss? Write it as a fraction of the whole flock.
The second loss is [[1/6]] of the REST — so [[1/6]] of what you found. Then [[5/6]] of that rest survives.
Survivors = [[5/6]] of [[6/7]]. “Of” means ×.

traps.0: That takes [[1/6]] away from the WHOLE flock. The second loss is [[1/6]] of the REST, which is [[6/7]] of the flock.
traps.2: [[5/6]] is only what survives the second loss. The first loss ([[1/7]]) happened too.
traps.3: [[6/7]] is what is left after the first year only. Don't forget the second loss.

solution: After year 1 the shepherd keeps [[6/7]] of the flock.
In year 2 he loses [[1/6]] of that rest, so he keeps [[5/6]] of the rest.
questions.idea: A fraction **of** a fraction: multiply. Work with the rest, not the whole.

questions.text:
Un berger a perdu le [[1/7]] de ses **56** chèvres l'an dernier et le [[1/6]] du reste cette année.
b) Combien de chèvres lui reste-t-il ?
hints: You already know the fraction that is left (part a).
Fraction left × the number of goats.
[[5/7]] of 56 — divide by 7 first, then × 5.

traps.0: 48 goats is what is left after only the first year (56 − 8).
traps.3: 8 is how many goats he lost EACH year (they happen to be equal). The question asks how many are LEFT.

solution: Check step by step: year 1 loses 8 → 48 left; year 2 loses [[1/6]] of 48 = 8 → **40** ✅
questions.idea: Find ONE piece first (56 ÷ 7), then count the pieces you keep.

hints: Brackets first — the INNERMOST ones. Two small calculations, each needs a common denominator.
( [[7/10]] + [[1/5]] ) = [[9/10]] and ( [[3/4]] − [[1/3]] ) = [[5/12]]. Multiply them to get the value of the big bracket.
The big bracket is [[3/8]]. Now [[1/5]] ÷ [[3/8]] means [[1/5]] × [[8/3]] — flip the second fraction — then subtract [[2/5]].

traps.0: [[8/15]] is [[1/5]] ÷ [[3/8]] — correct so far! But the last step, − [[2/5]], is still waiting.
traps.2: [[3/8]] is the value of the square bracket. You still have to divide [[1/5]] by it, then subtract [[2/5]].
traps.3: You multiplied [[1/5]] × [[3/8]]. Dividing by [[3/8]] means multiplying by the flipped fraction [[8/3]].

questions.idea: Brackets → × and ÷ → + and −. Dividing by a fraction = multiplying by its flip.

questions.text: a) Quelle fraction des animaux sont des poules ?
hints: Hens are “the rest” — what is left when you remove the other animals?
Add the fractions for pigs, rabbits and cows. Use a common denominator (30).

traps.0: [[5/6]] is the part that is NOT hens (pigs + rabbits + cows).
traps.3: [[2/15]] shows up twice in the story — it is the pigs' share, and the share of hens that lay well. Neither is the hens' share of the farm.

questions.idea: “The rest” = the whole (1) minus the parts.
questions.figure:
Monsieur Matheux possède une ferme sur laquelle on retrouve 450 animaux.
Les 2/15 animaux sont des cochons dont les 7/12 iront à l'abattoir cette semaine.
Les 3/10 des animaux sont des lapins et les 2/9 de ceux-ci sont noirs.
Les 2/5 des animaux sont des vaches. Malheureusement le 1/10 de ces vaches sont malades.
Le reste de ses animaux sont des poules. Monsieur Matheux considère que les 2/15 de ses poules sont de très bonnes pondeuses.

questions.text: b) Quelle fraction des animaux représentent les quadrupèdes ?
hints: Quadrupeds have FOUR legs. Which animals on this farm are they?
Pigs, rabbits and cows. Hens have two legs.
Add the three shares (denominator 30), or use 1 − hens.

traps.0: That leaves out the rabbits — rabbits are quadrupeds too.
traps.3: [[1/6]] is the hens' share — hens have only 2 legs.

questions.idea: Read the word: quadruped = 4 legs. Then choose the right groups.

questions.text: c) Quelle fraction des animaux sont des vaches malades ?
hints: Sick cows are a fraction of the COWS. Cows are a fraction of ALL the animals.
A fraction of a fraction → multiply.

traps.0: [[1/10]] is a fraction of the COWS, not of all the animals.

questions.idea: Fraction of WHAT? Here: [[1/10]] of the cows, not of the farm.

questions.text: d) Combien y a-t-il de vaches malades ?
hints: Use the fraction from part c.

traps.1: 180 is ALL the cows ([[2/5]] of 450). Only [[1/10]] of them are sick.
traps.2: 45 is [[1/10]] of ALL 450 animals. The sick fraction is of the cows.

questions.idea: Two roads, same answer — use one to check the other.

hints: Use the fraction of quadrupeds from part b.
450 ÷ 6 = 75 for each sixth; take 5 of them.

traps.0: 340 = 375 − 35. The 35 pigs go to the slaughterhouse in the FUTURE (“iront … cette semaine”) — they are still on the farm now.
traps.2: 75 is the number of HENS (one sixth). The quadrupeds are the other five sixths.

questions.idea: Divide by the denominator, multiply by the numerator.

questions.text: f) Les cochons et les poules représentent quelle fraction des animaux ?
hints: You already know both fractions (pigs: given; hens: part a).
Pigs [[2/15]] + hens [[1/6]]. Common denominator?

traps.0: That uses [[2/15]] for the hens too — but [[2/15]] is the share of hens that lay well. The hens' share of the farm is [[1/6]].
traps.2: You added the tops (2 + 1) and the bottoms (15 + 6). Fractions need a COMMON denominator first.
traps.3: [[5/6]] is all the quadrupeds, not pigs + hens.

questions.idea: Add fractions only when the pieces are the same size (common denominator).
